submission.natural_language_explanation: High side of a GELU-dip token-identity unit (the same neuron whose verified negative pole sits near the GELU minimum for most tokens): its activation is a fixed lookup on the current surface token - identical in every context and every syntactic role (' play' = 1.47 both as a verb and as a noun, ' make' = 1.46 after any prefix, 'making' = 1.48 across five unrelated registers), so the case form is a different token and matters (' door' 0.00 vs ' Door' 0.73, 'wish' 0.00 vs ' Wish' 0.94). It rises above zero only for a graded concrete everyday-action vocabulary: a top tier at 0.8-1.73 of the 1.729 max made of the generic activity verbs and their inflections (make/making/makes, do/does/doing, take/taking/took, play/playing/plays, watch, perform/performers, act, dance/dancers, hold/holding, render, wear) plus upper-case forms of several others (Cut, Hang, Pay, Pray, Wish); a mid tier at 0.4-0.8 of manual and leisure action verbs (draw, ride, skate, bake, roast, brew, chop, haul, cast, roll, conduct, practice, bend, cut, cook, hang); a scattering of animal/food nouns and capitalised names that no semantics predicts (' deer' 1.05 yet ' horse' 0.19, ' goose' 1.21 yet ' bird' 0.09, ' chess', Judith, Caesar); and one unexplained leftover, 'Even'/'even' (1.42/0.96). It is at zero on function words, on abstract/cognitive/communication verbs (think, know, want, say, tell, ask), on light and grammatical verbs (give, get, use, try, help, start, stop, find, put, look) and on concrete non-action nouns in their usual lower-case token (table, door, house, room, car, bread, soup).

rival_explanations: It is a generic verb (part-of-speech) detector rather than an action-semantics detector, so any verb token should fire and the zeros on think, know, give, get, use and walk are only weaknesses below the scan's active threshold.

It is only the handful of generic light activity verbs make/do/take/play/watch/perform/act/dance and their inflections, and the animals, food nouns, proper names and word fragments in the tail are embedding noise that will not replicate on new text.
It is a concrete-imageability unit whose real class is pictureable nouns and animals, with the activity verbs as the offshoot, so table, door, car and bread should fire as strongly as deer and goose.

The word on Editor Geek Street is that Sublime Text is The Business. Well, I think so too.
What particularly draws me to this swift, polished, accomplished, customisable and truly delectable editor is that it is cross platform. And as I'm still in the front end dev contracting game, this is a real boon: Mac, Windows or my own Minority Linux, I can have the same text editor across the board. Delight.
There is just so much goodness in there: Minimap, multi-pane editing, fully customizable key bindings, multiple selections, snippets, autocomplete, bracket-matching, bookmarks, text-folding and so many small, beautiful touches that it would make you weep if you found text editing romantic.
Tiny niggles aside, I suggest every last one of you take Sublime Text for a free trial spin, Operating System no object. Based on the passage above, Can you provide more information about the features of Sublime Text that make it a desirable text editor for front end development?<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>assistant
Sublime Text is a desirable text editor for front end development due to many reasons, some of which include:

1. Cross-platform compatibility: Sublime Text can be used across various operating systems such as Mac, Windows, and Linux, making it a convenient choice for developers who work on different machines.

2. Customizability: With its fully customizable key bindings, snippets, and autocomplete, Sublime Text allows front-end developers to tailor the editor to their preferences and workflow.

3. Multi-pane editing: The ability to edit multiple files side-by-side with its multi-pane editing feature assists developers in comparing and modifying code effectively.

4. Minimap: Sublime Text's minimap feature provides a bird's eye view of the code, facilitating quick navigation and pinpointing specific sections.

5. Bracket-matching: Front-end developers often work with nested and complex code structures; bracket-matching ensures that the opening and closing brackets are paired correctly, preventing errors and improving code quality.

6. Text-folding: Sublime Text's text-folding feature allows developers to collapse or hide blocks of code, providing a cleaner workspace and making it easier to focus on specific sections of the codebase.

7. Multiple selections: This feature enables developers to select multiple instances of the same code block and modify them simultaneously, saving time and increasing efficiency.

Overall, Sublime Text offers a range of features that are particularly useful for front-end developers, making it a popular choice in the industry.<|im_end|>

Summertime temperatures can pose a threat for all – especially the elderly. Due to how the body naturally changes with age, older adults are at greater risk for heat-related injuries. Society harps on young adults for the importance of sunscreen, staying hydrated and other health precautions during the warm season, but have we truly considered how rising temperatures drastically affect the elderly? AFC Urgent Care Springfield wants you to be educated on the preventive measures, symptoms and how to help a senior suffering from overexposure.
Avoiding skin damage is a hot topic for younger generations, however, age does not determine how much or how little you should be concerned about your skin. With time, skin becomes thinner and more sensitive, therefore more vulnerable. Not only can sunburn be painful, it increases a senior’s chance of excessive dryness, irritation or risk of skin cancer. Yes, these are common risks for any age, but older skin significantly loses the ability to protect itself from damages caused by ultraviolet (UV) rays. Applying both moisturizer and sunscreen should become a regular habit, and knowing when to stay inside or find the shade is crucial.
Consistent exposure to the sun without proper replenishment of fluids or rest will eventfully catch up with the body. Common symptomsof heat exhaustion include heavy sweating, cramps, dizziness, paleness and heavy breathing. Drinking cool, non-alcoholic beverages is a great way to prevent exhaustion – watch out for immensely cold liquids as they can result in cramping. Some seniors have strict doctors’ orders on how much liquid they can consume. If so, encourage them to talk with their doctor. If a senior must be outside during the hours of 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. (when temperatures are hottest) ensure they wear lightweight clothing and seek shade whenever possible.
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), along with other health organizations, agree that a heat stroke is the most critical heat-related illness. A heat stroke occurs when the body’s temperature rises rapidly due to an increase in the environment’s temperature, but at such a rate that the body cannot easily cool itself down. Unfortunately, it is more difficult for a senior’s body to regulate internal temperature, making them prone to a heat stroke if not cooled off immediately. It only takes about 10-15 minutes for the detrimental effects of a heat stroke to set in. A main indicator to watch for is when the body can no longer produce sweat.
How Can You Help in an Emergency?
AFC Urgent Care Springfield encourages you to remain aware of those around you during the sweltering summer heat. If you witness a senior experiencing any of the symptoms listed, please visit AFC Urgent Care Springfield for assistance.

You can help RHA prevent, manage and cure lung disease.
Policies that address air quality, asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), lung cancer and tobacco control help prevent, manage and cure lung disease. With your active engagement, RHA works to enact changes that will reduce youth smoking, help children with asthma manage their disease, and clean up our air for everyone who breathes. These changes benefit people living with lung disease today and generations to come.
Our advocacy successes are a reflection of the dedicated volunteers who make these efforts possible. Through your visits, calls and emails to legislators, elected officials learn what it is like to live with COPD, to manage a child’s asthma or to care for people living with lung cancer. Giving a voice to people living with lung disease is critical to introducing and passing lung-friendly policies.
With improved health outcomes and decreased costs to the health system, it is imperative to remember that protecting access to care is good for lung health. Respiratory Health Association’s issue brief, the Affordable Care Act is Good for Lung Health, examines how the ACA’s possible repeal will impact vulnerable populations, both locally and nationally, with a particular focus on the numbers who will lose their health care coverage. RHA will continue to advocate for access to care for the lung health community.
To better equip schools to handle asthma emergencies, RHA worked with public health partners to pass the Asthma Episode Emergency Response Protocol. This law ensures that uniform asthma response measures are in place in all Illinois schools and that all teachers have access to proper asthma management training and asthma emergency quick-reference documents. In collaboration with several state agencies, RHA developed an online training for school staff, which is accessible in our Asthma Management resources.
RHA and its allies helped secure passage of Illinois’ Future Energy Jobs Act, assuring greater use of renewable energy in the state and further reductions in air pollution from other energy sources — a law that will avoid thousands of asthma episodes. RHA continues to defend the funds that are dedicated to advancing clean, renewable energy in Illinois. Visit the Clean Energy section of our Library for additional information.
Respiratory Health Association applauds the National Heart Lung and Blood Institute and its partners for recognizing the need for a COPD National Action Plan. This plan will serve as a springboard for policy change that will help COPD patients and their caregivers, and foster better communications among healthcare providers, COPD caregivers, and patients, all in an effort to reduce the burden of COPD and improve health outcomes for people living with the disease. RHA worked for years with partners to urge federal leaders to develop the national action plan and we look forward to playing a key role in its implementation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The report of the council and its members is on the table in the room, and the car is outside.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Function words plus the hypothesis's zero-class concrete nouns (table, room, car) in ordinary lower-case form: no listed surface token is present, so a fixed token lookup should read zero while a pictureable-noun reading should fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: I think they know what we want, and we say nothing, because we can tell that it is better not to ask.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Dense abstract, cognitive and communication verbs from the hypothesis's zero list (think, know, want, say, tell, ask) with no action token, the case where a generic verb detector and the hypothesis disagree most sharply.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Please give me a hand, get the box, use the rope, try the lid, help the kids, find the key and put it there.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Nine light and grammatical verbs the hypothesis explicitly lists as zero (give, get, use, try, help, find, put) packed into imperative action commands, the hardest negative for a claim that excludes them by token identity.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She wiped the table, shut the door, left the house, tidied the room, parked the car, sliced the bread and stirred the soup.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Lower-case concrete non-action nouns (table, door, house, room, car, bread, soup) in a household scene: the hypothesis predicts zero for every one of them, the concrete-imageability rival predicts firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The horse stood by the fence while the bird sat on the gate, and neither moved for an hour.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The hypothesis's own sub-threshold animal counterexamples (horse 0.19, bird 0.09), both below its 0.4 mid-tier floor, in a barnyard scene a concrete-imageability unit should flag.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The maker of the film, the holder of the ticket and the actress met backstage after the performance.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Derivational near-misses of claimed lemmas (maker, holder, actress, performance) are different surface tokens from make/hold/act/perform, so the fixed lookup should read zero.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: El niño quería jugar en el parque, pero su madre le dijo que hiciera la tarea antes de la cena.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A Spanish action sentence with no English trigger token: a lookup on the listed surface forms should be silent whatever the sentence means, while a verb-POS reading may still fire on the Spanish verbs.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: A sense of doom hung over the doomed expedition as the dose of radiation spread through the camp.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tokens that begin with the letters of a trigger but are different surface tokens (doom, doomed, dose against ' do'), testing that the unit reads whole tokens rather than prefixes.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The parties hereby agree that the terms of this agreement shall govern all disputes between them and their successors.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Legal boilerplate of function words and unlisted relational verbs (agree, govern): no claimed activating token appears, so the hypothesis predicts zero.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She made a quiet promise to the group and kept it without any fuss.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The hypothesis's inflection list is make/making/makes, so ' made' is an unlisted surface token and the lookup should read zero even though the light-verb rival counts it as an inflection of make.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The evening was cool, and the streetlights came on one by one along the road.
adversarial_test_results.detail: ' evening' is a different surface token from the claimed leftover 'even', testing whether the unit keys on the whole token rather than a substring.

readings.explanation: High side of a GELU-dip token-identity unit (the same neuron whose verified negative pole sits near the GELU minimum for most tokens): its activation is a fixed lookup on the current surface token - identical in every context and every syntactic role (' play' = 1.47 both as a verb and as a noun, ' make' = 1.46 after any prefix, 'making' = 1.48 across five unrelated registers), so the case form is a different token and matters (' door' 0.00 vs ' Door' 0.73, 'wish' 0.00 vs ' Wish' 0.94). It rises above zero only for a graded concrete everyday-action vocabulary: a top tier at 0.8-1.73 of the 1.729 max made of the generic activity verbs and their inflections (make/making/makes, do/does/doing, take/taking/took, play/playing/plays, watch, perform/performers, act, dance/dancers, hold/holding, render, wear) plus upper-case forms of several others (Cut, Hang, Pay, Pray, Wish); a mid tier at 0.4-0.8 of manual and leisure action verbs (draw, ride, skate, bake, roast, brew, chop, haul, cast, roll, conduct, practice, bend, cut, cook, hang); a scattering of animal/food nouns and capitalised names that no semantics predicts (' deer' 1.05 yet ' horse' 0.19, ' goose' 1.21 yet ' bird' 0.09, ' chess', Judith, Caesar); and one unexplained leftover, 'Even'/'even' (1.42/0.96). It is at zero on function words, on abstract/cognitive/communication verbs (think, know, want, say, tell, ask), on light and grammatical verbs (give, get, use, try, help, start, stop, find, put, look) and on concrete non-action nouns in their usual lower-case token (table, door, house, room, car, bread, soup).

It is a generic verb (part-of-speech) detector rather than an action-semantics detector, so any verb token should fire and the zeros on think, know, give, get, use and walk are only weaknesses below the scan's active threshold.

It is only the handful of generic light activity verbs make/do/take/play/watch/perform/act/dance and their inflections, and the animals, food nouns, proper names and word fragments in the tail are embedding noise that will not replicate on new text.
It is a concrete-imageability unit whose real class is pictureable nouns and animals, with the activity verbs as the offshoot, so table, door, car and bread should fire as strongly as deer and goose.
